title: USMLE Step 3
issuer: National Board of Medical Examiners / FSMB
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public USMLE Step 3 content outline. Not a capture of past test questions.

items.stem: A 64-year-old man presents with 4 days of fever, chills, productive cough, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. Temperature is 38.9 C, blood pressure 104/66 mm Hg, heart rate 112/min, respiratory rate 26/min, and oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. Examination shows dullness to percussion at the right lung base with decreased breath sounds. A chest radiograph shows a right lower lobe infiltrate with a small adjacent pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Discharge home with oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and follow-up in one week
Admit for intravenous antibiotics and repeat chest imaging in 48 to 72 hours
Place a small-bore chest tube before any antibiotic therapy is started
Perform bronchoscopy to exclude an obstructing endobronchial lesion
items.explanation: Pneumonia with a parapneumonic effusion and borderline hemodynamics requires hospitalization with intravenous antibiotics and repeat imaging to decide whether the fluid needs drainage. Outpatient therapy is unsafe here, and drainage or bronchoscopy is premature before a trial of antibiotics.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 46-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after the sudden onset of the worst headache of her life with photophobia, nausea, and mild nuchal rigidity. She has no focal neurologic deficits. A non-contrast computed tomography of the head obtained 6 hours after symptom onset shows no hemorrhage. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Lumbar puncture to evaluate the cerebrospinal fluid for xanthochromia and red blood cells
Empiric antiviral therapy for possible viral encephalitis
Discharge with analgesics and a follow-up appointment in one week
Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging before any further testing
items.explanation: A negative non-contrast CT within the first 6 to 12 hours does not exclude subarachnoid hemorrhage, so lumbar puncture is required to look for xanthochromia or a traumatic tap with non-clearing red blood cells. Empiric antivirals, discharge, and delayed imaging would miss a ruptured aneurysm.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 70-year-old man with a history of inferior myocardial infarction presents 2 hours after the onset of crushing substernal chest pain. The electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Blood pressure is 96/60 mm Hg, heart rate is 54/min, and the jugular venous pressure is elevated. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management?
options: Administer sublingual nitroglycerin every 5 minutes for up to three doses
Give intravenous metoprolol to reduce myocardial oxygen demand before transfer
Delay treatment until cardiac enzyme results return in 2 hours
Activate primary percutaneous coronary intervention and give aspirin with a P2Y12 inhibitor
items.explanation: This is an inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction with findings suggesting right ventricular involvement, so nitrates and beta-blockers can precipitate profound hypotension. Immediate reperfusion with adjunctive antiplatelet therapy is the priority, and waiting for enzyme results wastes the treatment window.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 78-year-old woman from a nursing home is confused and reports dysuria. Temperature is 38.6 C, heart rate 118/min, blood pressure 92/58 mm Hg, and lactate is 3.1 mmol/L. Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Obtain a computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis before starting any antimicrobial
Obtain blood and urine cultures and give broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics with rapid crystalloid resuscitation
Start an oral fluoroquinolone and reassess in 48 hours
Await urine culture sensitivities before selecting an antibiotic
items.explanation: She meets criteria for sepsis with hypoperfusion, and the bundle for septic shock prevention includes cultures that do not delay therapy, prompt broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, and aggressive crystalloid resuscitation. Imaging, oral outpatient therapy, and waiting for sensitivities all delay time-critical treatment.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman reports palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss of 6 kg over 3 months, and a fine tremor of her hands. Heart rate is 132/min and irregular, blood pressure is 142/78 mm Hg, and the thyroid gland is diffusely enlarged without nodules. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic test?
options: Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone with reflex free thyroxine
Computed tomography of the head with pituitary protocol
Twenty-four hour urine collection for metanephrines and catecholamines
Trial of amiodarone with reassessment in two weeks
items.explanation: The presentation is compatible with newly recognized hyperthyroidism, and the thyroid-stimulating hormone level with reflex free thyroxine is the recommended first-line screening test. Pituitary imaging and urine metanephrines evaluate different disorders, and rate control without a diagnosis leaves the cause untreated.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 71-year-old woman who underwent hip replacement 3 weeks ago reports new right calf pain and swelling. The calf measures 3 cm larger than the left, the calf is tender to palpation, and her Wells score is assessed as moderate. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Begin warfarin alone and reassess the leg in 7 days
Wrap the leg with an elastic compression bandage and schedule an outpatient visit
Measure D-dimer and withhold all treatment if it is below the cutoff
Perform compression ultrasonography of the lower extremity veins
items.explanation: Recent major orthopedic surgery plus unilateral calf swelling gives a moderate pretest probability for deep vein thrombosis, so venous compression ultrasonography is the appropriate next test. The D-dimer strategy applies to low-probability patients, and anticoagulation should not start before the diagnosis is confirmed.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 14-year-old is seen for 2 days of fever, odynophagia, and white exudates on the pharynx without cough or coryza. There is tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy. A rapid antigen detection test is positive for group A Streptococcus. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Observe with antipyretics because a positive rapid test indicates a viral source
Obtain a throat culture and delay antibiotics for 48 hours regardless of symptoms
Treat with penicillin or amoxicillin for 10 days to prevent acute rheumatic fever
Use cephalexin twice daily as the routine first-line regimen for every patient
items.explanation: A positive rapid antigen test in a patient with compatible symptoms confirms group A streptococcal pharyngitis, which is treated with penicillin or amoxicillin for 10 days to prevent acute rheumatic fever and suppurative complications. A positive test is not viral, culture is used to confirm negative rapid tests, and cephalosporins are reserved for penicillin-allergic patients.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 60-year-old man reports 2 months of progressive difficulty swallowing solids, unintentional weight loss of 7 kg, and intermittent regurgitation of food. He has no history of caustic ingestion or chronic reflux disease. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Upper endoscopy with biopsy of any visible mucosal abnormality
Computed tomography of the abdomen to evaluate for a pancreatic mass
Barium swallow as the only initial investigation
Eight-week trial of a proton pump inhibitor before further workup
items.explanation: Progressive dysphagia to solids with weight loss in an older adult is alarm symptomatology for esophageal cancer, so esophagogastroduodenoscopy with biopsy is the definitive first investigation. Cross-sectional imaging does not inspect the lumen, a barium study cannot obtain tissue, and empiric acid suppression ignores the red flags.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 76-year-old woman on postoperative day 2 after repair of a hip fracture becomes acutely confused, pulls at her intravenous line, and is more disoriented at night. She is afebrile, oxygen saturation is 96%, and her only new medication is an opioid analgesic. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?
options: Apply full physical restraints continuously and give no analgesia
Start daily haloperidol for the remainder of the admission as prophylaxis
Obtain emergent magnetic resonance imaging of the brain to exclude metastatic disease
Assess for reversible causes such as pain, infection, and medication effects while using oriented, nonpharmacologic measures
items.explanation: Acute postoperative confusion is managed by searching for precipitants, including uncontrolled pain, hypoxia, infection, and newly added drugs, along with orienting cues, sleep hygiene, and family presence. Continuous restraints can worsen outcomes and increase falls, and routine antipsychotic prophylaxis has no role in a reversible delirium.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 19-year-old with type 1 diabetes mellitus presents with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She breathes deeply and rapidly, her breath smells fruity, glucose is 486 mg/dL, serum bicarbonate is 8 mEq/L, and arterial pH is 7.14. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial therapy?
options: Begin an insulin infusion without checking the serum potassium
Give sodium bicarbonate as a bolus to normalize the pH immediately
Administer dextrose before any insulin is given
Give intravenous normal saline followed by insulin with potassium replaced when indicated
items.explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis is treated with volume repletion first, then continuous insulin infusion, with potassium monitored and replaced before it falls dangerously. Giving insulin before fluids can precipitate shock, bicarbonate is reserved for severe acidemia with hyperkalemia, and dextrose is added only once the glucose falls.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 66-year-old with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is brought to the emergency department with increased dyspnea and purulent sputum. Respiratory rate is 30/min, he speaks in short phrases, oxygen saturation is 82% on room air, pH is 7.28, and partial pressure of carbon dioxide is 72 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Discharge home with nebulized bronchodilators and an oral antibiotic
Intubate immediately without attempting any less invasive support
Start noninvasive ventilation with controlled oxygen plus systemic corticosteroids and antibiotics
Give a bronchodilator alone and reassess after one hour in the waiting room
items.explanation: Severe hypoxemia with respiratory acidosis and hypercapnia during an exacerbation, in a patient who is awake and protecting his airway, is an indication for immediate noninvasive ventilation together with controlled oxygen, corticosteroids, and antibiotics. Intubation is reserved for failure or contraindications to noninvasive support.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 22-year-old college student presents with temperature of 39.4 C, severe headache, neck stiffness, and a petechial rash over the trunk and lower extremities. Blood pressure is 98/60 mm Hg, heart rate is 118/min, and he is confused. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action?
options: Arrange outpatient treatment after the rash resolves
Administer intravenous ceftriaxone at once and give chemoprophylaxis to close contacts
Wait for lumbar puncture and culture results before starting therapy
Give dexamethasone alone for 72 hours before any antimicrobial
items.explanation: Suspected meningococcal sepsis is a medical emergency, so empiric third-generation cephalosporin therapy must not be delayed for lumbar puncture or culture results, and antimicrobial chemoprophylaxis is given to close contacts. Corticosteroids are an adjunct with antibiotics, never a substitute for them.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 58-year-old man with cirrhosis from alcohol use disorder develops increasing abdominal distension, fever, and diffuse abdominal tenderness over 2 days. He is tachycardic, and the scrotum is edematous. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Diagnostic paracentesis with cell count, differential, albumin, and culture
Increase the dose of furosemide and spironolactone
Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis before any fluid is sampled
Observe for 48 hours to see whether the fever resolves
items.explanation: A patient with cirrhosis and new ascites plus fever or abdominal pain requires urgent diagnostic paracentesis to diagnose spontaneous bacterial peritonosis and to guide therapy. Diuretics treat volume, not infection, and imaging or observation delays a time-sensitive diagnosis.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 66-year-old woman is witnessed to have acute right-sided weakness and expressive aphasia. Last known well was 90 minutes ago. Non-contrast computed tomography of the head shows no hemorrhage or early ischemic change, and blood pressure is 178/104 mm Hg. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Give intravenous alteplase after confirming there is no intracranial hemorrhage
Lower the blood pressure to below 120/80 mm Hg before reperfusion therapy
Give aspirin alone and reassess the neurologic examination in 24 hours
Withhold thrombolysis and proceed directly to endovascular thrombectomy without intravenous treatment
items.explanation: She is inside the treatment window, her blood pressure is below the 185/110 mm Hg threshold, and imaging excludes hemorrhage, so intravenous thrombolysis is indicated now. Excessive blood pressure lowering risks worsening the penumbra, and withholding reperfusion to await deterioration is not appropriate.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman with a history of asthma comes to the emergency department 30 minutes after exposure to a strong odor. She can speak only in single words, respiratory rate is 34/min, oxygen saturation is 90%, peak expiratory flow is 35% of predicted, and expiratory wheezing is audible. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Discharge with an inhaled corticosteroid and routine follow-up
Give an oral antihistamine and observe for one hour
Give nebulized magnesium and prepare for discharge once peak flow reaches 70%
Give continuous inhaled bronchodilators with systemic corticosteroids and prepare for ventilatory support if she worsens
items.explanation: Inability to speak in sentences, hypoxemia, and peak flow well below 50% of predicted define a life-threatening asthma exacerbation that requires continuous bronchodilators, early systemic corticosteroids, frequent reassessment, and readiness for noninvasive or invasive ventilatory support.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 54-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with sudden severe tearing pain radiating to his back that began 1 hour ago. Blood pressure is 212/118 mm Hg in both arms, heart rate is 96/min, and neurologic examination is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic test?
options: D-dimer to exclude pulmonary embolism
Exercise stress testing to evaluate for myocardial ischemia
Computed tomography angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Transthoracic echocardiography alone as the definitive study
items.explanation: Abrupt tearing pain radiating to the back with marked hypertension and equal bilateral pressures is classic for acute aortic syndrome, and CT angiography from chest through pelvis is the rapid, definitive initial study. Stress testing and D-dimer address different processes, and echocardiography can miss distal disease.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 9-year-old boy develops diffuse urticaria, facial swelling, and wheeze 15 minutes after eating a peanut butter sandwich. He is hoarse, his voice is muffled, blood pressure is 82/50 mm Hg, and he is struggling to breathe. Which of the following is the most appropriate first treatment?
options: Oral diphenhydramine and observation
Intramuscular epinephrine into the lateral thigh
Intravenous normal saline bolus before any medication is given
Nebulized albuterol with an oral corticosteroid
items.explanation: Anaphylaxis with airway compromise and hypotension is treated first with intramuscular epinephrine, the only intervention that reliably reverses the pathophysiologic cascade. Antihistamines, fluids, bronchodilators, and corticosteroids are adjuncts and must not delay epinephrine.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 63-year-old man with stage 4 chronic kidney disease and poor adherence to follow-up is found to have a serum potassium of 6.4 mEq/L. He reports muscle weakness, and the electrocardiogram shows peaked T waves without QRS widening. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Repeat the serum potassium in 24 hours without intervention
Give intravenous calcium gluconate, insulin with dextrose, and nebulized albuterol while arranging renal replacement therapy
Start an oral potassium binder alone and discharge home
Obtain an emergent computed tomography of the head because peaked T waves indicate a central cause
items.explanation: Symptomatic hyperkalemia with electrocardiographic changes is an emergency managed in parallel with membrane stabilization using intracellular shift by insulin, glucose, and beta-agonists, plus removal of potassium with urgent dialysis in advanced kidney disease. Delayed oral therapy alone can be fatal.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 70-year-old man admitted with pneumonia develops abrupt palpitations. He is confused and diaphoretic, heart rate is 156/min and irregular, blood pressure is 86/58 mm Hg, and the electrocardiogram shows atrial fibrillation. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
options: Synchronized electrical cardioversion
Oral metoprolol twice daily with outpatient cardiology referral
Observation with a repeat electrocardiogram in 6 hours
Intravenous digoxin while awaiting the serum potassium result
items.explanation: Atrial fibrillation with hemodynamic instability, shown by hypotension, confusion, and diaphoresis, requires immediate synchronized cardioversion. Slow oral rate control, observation, and awaiting laboratory results are inappropriate in an unstable patient, and digoxin acts too slowly.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 31-year-old woman at 30 weeks of gestation presents with a severe headache, visual changes, and epigastric pain. Blood pressure is 172/112 mm Hg on two readings, urine protein is 3+, deep tendon reflexes are brisk, and the fetal heart rate is normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Give magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis and plan definitive delivery
Start oral labetalol alone and arrange follow-up in one week
Await a repeat blood pressure measurement in 7 days
Begin low-dose aspirin and observation
items.explanation: Severe features of preeclampsia require immediate magnesium sulfate to prevent eclampsia, rapid blood pressure control, and timely delivery planning. Weekly outpatient monitoring is unsafe, and aspirin is used for prevention earlier in gestation rather than as treatment of an established severe syndrome.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Patient Management and Clinical Judgment

items.stem: A 54-year-old woman who has been taking phenelzine for treatment-resistant depression eats aged cheese and cured sausage, then develops a severe occipital headache, blood pressure of 208/122 mm Hg, nausea, and sweating. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Double the dose of the antidepressant and reassure the patient
Give an oral beta blocker alone and send the patient home
Administer an antihistamine and observe for 2 hours
Remove the dietary trigger and lower the pressure with a rapidly acting agent such as intravenous phentolamine or nitroprusside
items.explanation: This is a sympathomimetic crisis caused by tyramine in fermented foods interacting with a monoamine oxidase inhibitor, and it is treated by removing the trigger and lowering blood pressure with a rapidly titratable agent. Beta-blockade alone can worsen the pressure through unopposed alpha stimulation.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 68-year-old man with atrial fibrillation has had a stable international normalized ratio of 2.4 on warfarin. He completes 5 days of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection, and today's INR is 6.1 with no bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Continue warfarin at the same dose and repeat the INR in 30 days
Give intravenous vitamin K 10 mg daily for one month
Hold warfarin, give low-dose oral vitamin K, and recheck the INR frequently
Transfuse platelets and continue anticoagulation unchanged
items.explanation: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole potentiates warfarin, and an INR above 6 without bleeding calls for holding the drug with a small oral vitamin K dose and close monitoring. High-dose vitamin K overcorrects and makes re-anticoagulation difficult, while platelet transfusion does nothing for a coagulation factor deficiency.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman started on lamotrigine 3 weeks ago for bipolar disorder returns with fever, a morbilliform rash on the face and trunk, facial edema, painful mouth sores, and enlarged cervical lymph nodes. Laboratory studies show lymphocytosis with atypical lymphocytes and mild transaminase elevation. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Add a topical corticosteroid and increase the lamotrigine dose
Stop lamotrigine immediately and never rechallenge
Give diphenhydramine and continue the medication at the current dose
Reduce the dose by half and complete a slower titration
items.explanation: Fever, rash, facial edema, mucosal involvement, lymphadenopathy, and liver injury within the first weeks of lamotrigine suggest a severe hypersensitivity reaction such as DRESS or Stevens-Johnson syndrome. The drug must be stopped permanently, and rechallenge can be fatal.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: An 8-year-old boy has asthma that has been controlled on as-needed albuterol, but he now uses it 4 days per week and awakens twice a month at night. Examination is normal, and he has had no exacerbations requiring systemic corticosteroids in the past year. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in therapy?
options: A long-acting muscarinic antagonist as the sole controller medication
A daily oral leukotriene receptor antagonist as the only controller
More frequent use of the as-needed short-acting beta agonist alone
A low-dose inhaled corticosteroid given daily plus as-needed albuterol for relief
items.explanation: Symptoms more than twice a week and nocturnal awakenings indicate mild persistent asthma, for which daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid therapy is the preferred controller with a short-acting beta agonist for quick relief. A long-acting bronchodilator without an inhaled steroid is not recommended as sole therapy.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 67-year-old woman who is 5 years postmenopausal is found to have a lumbar spine T-score of minus 3.1 and a hip T-score of minus 2.6. She has no prior fractures, no glucocorticoid use, and adequate calcium and vitamin D intake. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Calcium 500 mg daily with no other therapy
Repeat densitometry in 5 years without intervention
An antiresorptive medication such as alendronate or denosumab with calcium and vitamin D
A course of systemic corticosteroids to preserve bone density
items.explanation: A spine T-score of minus 3.1 establishes osteoporosis, and pharmacologic therapy with a bisphosphonate or denosumab plus adequate calcium and vitamin D is indicated to reduce fracture risk. Observation allows further bone loss, and glucocorticoids accelerate it.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman at 10 weeks of gestation presents with dysuria, urinary frequency, and suprapubic discomfort. She has no fever or flank pain, and urine cultures are pending. Which of the following is the most appropriate empiric antibiotic?
options: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole as the preferred agent in the first trimester
Nitrofurantoin or cephalexin, which are acceptable in early pregnancy
Ciprofloxacin because fluoroquinolones concentrate well in the urine
Doxycycline until culture and sensitivity results return
items.explanation: Uncomplicated cystitis in the first trimester is treated empirically with nitrofurantoin or a first-generation cephalosporin. Trimethoprim is avoided early in pregnancy because of folate antagonism, and fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines are avoided throughout pregnancy.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 48-year-old man has 3 weeks of mechanical low back pain after lifting boxes. He has no fever, no weight loss, no bowel or bladder dysfunction, and a normal neurologic examination with a negative straight leg raise. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, activity modification, and reassurance with planned reassessment
An opioid prescription for 30 days to prevent chronic pain
Strict bed rest with spinal immobilization for 6 weeks
Empiric antibiotics for suspected vertebral osteomyelitis
items.explanation: Mechanical low back pain without red flags is managed supportively with nonopioid analgesia, early activity, and patient education. Prolonged opioids risk dependence without added benefit, immobilization delays recovery, and antibiotics are indicated only when infection is suspected.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 58-year-old man with chronic kidney disease stage 3B and chronic tophaceous gout presents with an acutely inflamed, warm, and extremely tender first metatarsophalangeal joint. Serum creatinine is 2.4 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for the acute flare?
options: Naproxen 500 mg twice daily for 14 days
Colchicine at a standard high loading dose without any renal adjustment
Intra-articular corticosteroid injection or a short course of oral prednisone
High-dose allopurinol started today to treat both the flare and the underlying disease
items.explanation: Advanced chronic kidney disease makes nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs hazardous, and colchicine requires renal dose adjustment, so an intra-articular or short systemic corticosteroid course is the safest treatment for the flare. Urate-lowering therapy is titrated separately after the acute episode resolves.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 70-year-old man with stable coronary artery disease takes aspirin 81 mg daily and ibuprofen 600 mg three times a day for osteoarthritis. His serum creatinine has risen from 1.1 to 1.9 mg/dL over 3 months, and he has dyspepsia. Which of the following is the most appropriate medication change?
options: Increase the ibuprofen dose for improved analgesic effect
Stop the ibuprofen and use acetaminophen with a topical anti-inflammatory instead
Add a second proton pump inhibitor and continue the ibuprofen unchanged
Switch aspirin to clopidogrel because it has no renal effects
items.explanation: Chronic high-dose ibuprofen causes nephrotoxicity, can blunt the cardioprotection of aspirin, and aggravates dyspepsia, so it should be replaced with acetaminophen and a topical agent. Adding a second acid suppressant does not address the kidney injury, and changing antiplatelet therapy is unnecessary.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 30-year-old man reports intravenous use of oxycodone for 3 years and asks for help stopping. He last used 20 hours ago and has myalgias, rhinorrhea, yawning, and dilated pupils, with no medical contraindications to agonist therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment plan?
options: Withdrawal support with clonidine alone and discharge to outpatient counseling
Initiate buprenorphine-naloxone or methadone maintenance combined with behavioral therapy
Treat the withdrawal with a short course of benzodiazepines for 7 days
Arrange admission for a 30-day supervised taper with no maintenance medication
items.explanation: Opioid use disorder is best treated with medication for opioid use disorder, such as buprenorphine or methadone, together with behavioral therapy, which reduces relapse and mortality. Alpha-2 agonists alone, benzodiazepine tapers, and unsupported withdrawal carry much higher relapse rates.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 36-year-old man with treatment-resistant schizophrenia is started on clozapine after failing two other antipsychotics, and therapy is expected to continue indefinitely. Which of the following monitoring requirements is essential during the early months of therapy?
options: Frequent absolute neutrophil count monitoring before each dose during the initial period
Monthly echocardiography for the first year of therapy
Weekly serum lithium concentrations
Serial electroencephalograms before each refill
items.explanation: Clozapine carries a risk of severe neutropenia, so the absolute neutrophil count is checked before each dose during the first months and then at intervals defined by the risk evaluation program. The other monitoring tests apply to different drugs, not to clozapine.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 60-year-old man with a mechanical mitral valve on warfarin is scheduled for an elective cholecystectomy in 5 days. His most recent international normalized ratio is 3.0 and he has no bleeding history. Which of the following is the most appropriate perioperative anticoagulation plan?
options: Stop warfarin 10 days before surgery with no bridging therapy
Continue warfarin through the operation without interruption
Use aspirin alone throughout the perioperative period
Hold warfarin and bridge with heparin until the procedure, then resume warfarin promptly after hemostasis
items.explanation: A mechanical mitral valve is a high-risk indication for thromboembolism, so warfarin is held close to surgery and bridged with unfractionated or low-molecular-weight heparin, with anticoagulation restarted once surgical hemostasis is secure. Unbridged interruption and aspirin alone risk valve thrombosis.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 2-year-old boy ingests a bottle of ferrous sulfate tablets 90 minutes ago. He is vomiting and lethargic, with a serum glucose of 45 mg/dL. Abdominal radiograph shows multiple radio-opaque tablets in the stomach. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Activated charcoal in every case regardless of the time since ingestion
Observation only with a single iron level drawn in 12 hours
Whole bowel irrigation plus deferoxamine if systemic toxicity or persistent radiopaque density is present
N-acetylcysteine for hepatic protection
items.explanation: Symptomatic iron ingestion with retained radiopaque tablets requires decontamination with whole bowel irrigation and chelation with deferoxamine once systemic toxicity is evident. Activated charcoal does not bind iron well, observation alone is unsafe, and N-acetylcysteine treats acetaminophen overdose.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, albuminuria of 300 mg per day, and hypertension has a blood pressure of 152/94 mm Hg despite lifestyle measures. Potassium is normal and creatinine is 1.3 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate antihypertensive?
options: A non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker as monotherapy
Metoprolol as the first-choice agent
An angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker
Hydralazine twice daily as initial therapy
items.explanation: An ACE inhibitor or ARB is preferred in a patient with diabetes and albuminuria because it slows the progression of diabetic kidney disease in addition to lowering blood pressure. Beta-blockers and hydralazine are not first-line for this indication, and a calcium channel blocker does not provide the same renoprotection.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 9 weeks of gestation has a new diagnosis of Graves disease with a free thyroxine twice the upper limit of normal and a suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone. She has no cardiac symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacologic therapy?
options: Radioactive iodine ablation for rapid definitive control
Propylthiouracil at the lowest effective dose during the first trimester
Methimazole throughout pregnancy regardless of gestational age
No treatment until after delivery in every case
items.explanation: Thionamides are used to control hyperthyroidism in pregnancy, and propylthiouracil is preferred during the first trimester because of concerns about methimazole-related embryopathy, using the lowest dose that keeps free hormone levels near normal. Radioactive iodine is contraindicated in pregnancy, and untreated disease risks fetal growth restriction.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Pharmacology and Therapeutics

items.stem: A new screening test for a disease with a prevalence of 1% in the screened population has a sensitivity of 90% and a specificity of 90%. Among people who test positive, what is the most likely positive predictive value?
options: Approximately 8 percent
Approximately 50 percent
Approximately 90 percent
Approximately 99 percent
items.explanation: In 10,000 people, 100 have the disease and 90 of them test positive, while about 990 of the 9,900 without disease also test positive. The positive predictive value is therefore 90 divided by 1,080, which is about 8 percent, showing how low prevalence drives false positives.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: Investigators identify 400 patients with a rare leukemia subtype through cancer registries and then use occupational records to determine how often each had previously worked in pesticide application compared with matched people who do not have cancer. Which study design is this?
options: Randomized controlled clinical trial
Cross-sectional population survey
Uncontrolled case series
Case-control study with matched controls
items.explanation: Participants are selected by disease status and prior exposure is ascertained afterward, which defines a case-control study, with matching used to improve comparability. A cross-sectional survey would sample the population without regard to disease status, and a case series has no comparison group.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: In a case-control study of pancreatic cancer, the odds of ever smoking among patients with the cancer are 3 times the odds among matched controls. Which interpretation of the odds ratio of 3.0 is correct?
options: Smoking increases the absolute risk of pancreatic cancer by 3 percent
Smoking increases the relative risk of pancreatic cancer by 300 percent in this population
Three percent of patients with pancreatic cancer can be attributed to smoking
The odds of prior smoking among cases are 3 times those among controls, which approximates the relative risk when the disease is rare
items.explanation: An odds ratio compares exposure odds in cases with exposure odds in controls; it does not give an absolute risk, an attributable fraction, or a percentage increase in relative risk. When the disease is rare, the odds ratio reasonably approximates the risk ratio.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: A randomized trial compares a new antihypertensive with placebo and reports a between-group difference with a p value of 0.03. Which statement best describes what this p value means?
options: There is a 3 percent probability that the null hypothesis is true
The new drug produced a clinically important improvement in 97 percent of participants
If there were truly no difference, results at least this extreme would occur about 3 times in 100 repetitions, meeting the 0.05 threshold
The trial enrolled a sample large enough to detect a 3 percent difference
items.explanation: A p value is the probability of observing results at least as extreme as those obtained, assuming the null hypothesis is true. It is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true, and it says nothing about effect size, clinical importance, or power.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: An observational study reports that coffee drinkers have higher rates of pancreatic cancer than non-drinkers. Coffee drinkers in the cohort also smoke more cigarettes and consume more alcohol, and after statistical adjustment for those factors the association is no longer present. Which explanation is best?
options: Recall bias caused by inaccurate reporting of coffee intake
Selection bias caused by participants who declined to enroll
Confounding by smoking and alcohol use, which accounted for the observed association
Random error resulting from an inadequate sample size
items.explanation: A variable associated with both the exposure and the outcome that can account for the observed relationship is a confounder. Here adjustment eliminated the association, indicating that smoking and alcohol, rather than coffee, explained the initial finding.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: Over 5 years, a new medication reduces myocardial infarctions from 160 to 120 per 1,000 treated patients compared with placebo. What is the number needed to treat to prevent one myocardial infarction over 5 years?
items.explanation: The absolute risk reduction is 40 per 1,000, which is 4 percent, and the number needed to treat equals 1 divided by 0.04, giving 25 patients treated for 5 years to prevent one myocardial infarction.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: Over 20 years, a national survey finds that the prevalence of type 2 diabetes has doubled, while the annual incidence has changed little and average survival after diagnosis has lengthened. Which statement best explains these findings?
options: Longer disease duration and improved survival raise prevalence even when few new cases occur
Prevalence must rise whenever incidence is unchanged
Screening does not affect measured prevalence in any population
A doubling of prevalence proves that incidence doubled as well
items.explanation: Prevalence depends on both the rate of new cases and how long people live with the disease, so improved survival increases prevalence even when incidence is stable. Incidence and prevalence are distinct measures, and screening does influence how many prevalent cases are detected.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: A phase II oncology study treats 35 patients with an advanced solid tumor using a single investigational agent and reports a 40% radiographic response rate. Which limitation most affects the strength of this conclusion?
options: The sample of 35 patients is larger than a phase II study should enroll
Randomization cannot be performed in any oncology study
Tumor response measured by imaging is an objective outcome
Without a comparison group, regression to the mean and natural history cannot be excluded
items.explanation: A single-arm design cannot distinguish a treatment effect from the tumor's natural history or spontaneous regression, so a control group is required before efficacy can be claimed. Imaging-based response is objective, but it does not compensate for the missing comparator.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: In a primary care clinic where the prevalence of a particular infection is 2%, a rapid test has a sensitivity of 95% and a specificity of 90%. Which use of the test result is best supported by these characteristics?
options: Confirming the diagnosis in a high-risk symptomatic population when the result is positive
Excluding the infection when the result is negative in this low-prevalence setting
Replacing the confirmatory culture for every patient
Raising the positive predictive value by repeating the test in rapid succession
items.explanation: With low prevalence, most positive results are false, so the positive predictive value is poor while the negative predictive value is very high. The test is therefore best used to rule out infection when negative rather than to confirm disease when positive.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: A health department is considering a screening program for a condition with a prevalence of 1 in 100,000, no effective treatment, and an expensive universal screening test with moderate false-positive rates. Which consideration most argues against screening?
options: Screening a very rare untreated condition with a costly test yields mostly false positives and no benefit
The condition has a well-characterized natural history and a detectable latent phase
An effective treatment exists that reduces mortality when started early
A simple, inexpensive, and accurate screening test is available
items.explanation: Screening is justified when the condition is important, detectable before symptoms, and treatable in a way that improves outcomes. A rare disease without effective treatment, screened with a costly imperfect test, produces false positives and anxiety while offering no survival benefit.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: A randomized trial of a new oncologic drug reports a hazard ratio for death of 0.70 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.55 to 0.89 and a p value of 0.004. Which interpretation is most accurate?
options: The drug reduced the chance of death by exactly 30 percent for every participant
The result is not statistically significant because the interval crosses 1
There is a 0.4 percent probability that the drug has no effect whatsoever
The hazard of death was about 30 percent lower with the drug, and the interval excluding 1 indicates a statistically significant benefit
items.explanation: A hazard ratio of 0.70 indicates roughly a 30 percent relative reduction in the instantaneous hazard of death. Because the 95% confidence interval does not include 1 and the p value is below 0.05, the result is statistically significant, and the interval shows the plausible range around the estimate.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: In a study of birth defects, trained interviewers ask mothers of infants with congenital heart defects and mothers of healthy infants about medication, alcohol, and dietary exposures during pregnancy. Mothers of affected infants report exposures far more often than mothers of controls. Which type of bias is most likely operating?
options: Lead-time bias from earlier detection of disease
Surveillance bias from unequal monitoring intensity
Recall bias that can inflate the apparent exposure association
Attrition bias caused by participants lost to follow-up
items.explanation: When knowledge of the outcome influences how completely exposure information is recalled, differences in reporting can exaggerate associations. This recall bias is minimized by using medical records or interviewers blinded to outcome status.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: Town A has a higher crude death rate than Town B, but after age adjustment to a standard population, Town A's death rate is lower than Town B's. Town A has a much older population. Which conclusion is best?
options: Once age structure is standardized, fewer deaths occur in Town A than in Town B
Age adjustment cannot be applied to populations of different sizes
Town B has the lower underlying mortality rate at every age
The two rates use different numerators and cannot be compared
items.explanation: Crude rates are distorted when age structures differ, and standardization shows that Town A's higher crude rate reflects its older population rather than higher risk at each age. The age-specific rates themselves are not given, so no conclusion about every age group can be drawn.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Biostatistics and Epidemiology

items.stem: A 78-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment is offered an operation to repair an abdominal aortic aneurysm. He accurately states his diagnosis, the recommended procedure, its risks and benefits, and the likely outcome if he refuses, and his decision matches statements he made years earlier. He declines the operation. Which of the following is most appropriate?
options: Proceed with the operation because impaired cognition invalidates his refusal
Obtain consent from a relative who is willing to authorize the surgery
Sedate the patient so that treatment can proceed as recommended
Respect his informed refusal while continuing to offer information and revisit the discussion
items.explanation: Decision-making capacity requires understanding, appreciating, reasoning, and communicating a choice, all of which this patient demonstrates. An informed refusal must be honored even when the physician and family disagree, provided he retains capacity for this decision.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A 52-year-old man in the emergency department with a confirmed pulmonary embolism and hypoxemia insists on leaving against medical advice to attend a family event. He is fully oriented and understands that he may die if he leaves. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
options: Restrain him until a family member arrives to consent to treatment
Escort him out immediately without further discussion
Petition a court to override his decision before he leaves
Explore his concerns, explain the specific risks, document the discussion, and tell him he may return at any time
items.explanation: A competent patient may refuse treatment even when the refusal is unwise. The physician should elicit the reasons, communicate the specific risks in plain terms, document the conversation, and keep the door open for return rather than restraining, abandoning, or coercing the patient.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A 64-year-old man with advanced dementia and no written advance directive develops a bleeding ulcer. His adult daughter is his legally recognized surrogate and must decide whether to authorize transfusion. Which principle should guide her decision?
options: The choice an average patient in the same situation would make
The option that is least costly for the family and the hospital
Substituted judgment based on his previously expressed wishes, or, if unknown, his best interests
Her own religious convictions regardless of what her father valued
items.explanation: Surrogates act as substitutes for the patient's own voice, using the patient's known values and wishes first and a best-interest standard when those are unknown. Substituting the surrogate's preferences, an average patient standard, or cost is not the ethical standard for surrogate decision making.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A 67-year-old woman hospitalized for pneumonia develops profuse watery diarrhea on hospital day 5 and tests positive for toxigenic Clostridioides difficile. Which infection control precaution is most appropriate?
options: Droplet precautions for 5 days after therapy begins
Contact precautions with a private room and hand hygiene using soap and water
Airborne precautions with an N95 respirator for all staff
No precautions once the diarrhea improves
items.explanation: Clostridioides difficile requires contact precautions with a private room or cohorting plus gloves and gowns, and hands must be washed with soap and water because alcohol-based gel does not remove spores. The patient remains a transmission risk until diarrhea resolves.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: During a laparoscopic procedure, a surgeon inadvertently incises the ureter, recognizes it immediately, and repairs it over a stent without complication. The patient recovers normally and asks how the operation went. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
options: Disclose the complication promptly with an apology and a clear plan for follow-up care
Withhold the information because the patient recovered without harm
Wait until the patient asks a more specific question about the repair
Record the event only in a confidential quality report and say nothing
items.explanation: Ethical and professional standards require timely disclosure of unanticipated events with an apology and an explanation of the plan of care. Transparency supports trust, and institutional reporting supplements rather than replaces disclosure to the patient.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A 71-year-old with sepsis is transferred from the intensive care unit to a medical ward after 48 hours of stability. Two blood culture sets remain pending, and his antibiotic was changed that morning. Which handoff practice most reduces the risk of an adverse event after transfer?
options: A structured face-to-face handoff covering pending results, medication changes, and explicit read-back by the receiver
A verbal summary given in the hallway without written documentation
Reliance on the electronic record alone with no direct conversation
Asking the patient's family to relay critical information to the ward team
items.explanation: A structured handoff with closed-loop confirmation ensures that pending results, medication changes, and the plan are transmitted accurately and understood by the receiving team. Informal verbal updates, record-only transfers, and family intermediaries omit critical details and invite error.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A hospital finds that two patients received ten times the intended dose of a weight-based heparin infusion because residents wrote free-text doses on paper orders. A root cause analysis is convened. Which intervention is most likely to prevent recurrence?
options: Written warning letters to the residents involved
Retraining on the same free-text ordering process
Adding a second nurse to verify the existing paper order
A standardized weight-based computerized order set with dose limits and alerts
items.explanation: System redesign with forcing functions, standardized protocols, and dose-limit alerts addresses the conditions that produced the error. Punitive letters, retraining on the same flawed process, and additional manual verification steps are less reliable at preventing recurrence.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A 64-year-old man is found to have metastatic pancreatic cancer. He asks his oncologist not to be told further details and to provide all information to his wife instead. He is fully competent. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach?
options: Tell him everything immediately because the diagnosis concerns him most
Provide no information to him at all for the remainder of his illness
Respect his wishes about disclosure while exploring how much he wants to know and revisiting as circumstances change
Decline to discuss the diagnosis with anyone until he loses capacity
items.explanation: A competent patient may direct how information is shared, and the physician should honor that preference while continuing to ask how much the patient wishes to know, because preferences about disclosure often evolve as the illness progresses. Total nondisclosure or forced disclosure ignores patient autonomy.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A nurse catches an order for a medication at ten times the intended dose before it is administered, so no patient is harmed. The pharmacy and the clinical team are notified. Which next step best supports a culture of safety?
options: Publicly discipline the prescriber to deter similar errors
Submit a nonpunitive event report and analyze the system factors involved
File no report because the patient was not harmed
Notify the state licensing board before any internal review occurs
items.explanation: Near misses are valuable signals, and nonpunitive reporting systems capture them so system causes can be addressed before harm occurs. Punishing individuals suppresses reporting, and the absence of harm does not exempt an event from internal analysis.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A 34-year-old man being evaluated in an urgent psychiatric setting states that he will shoot his former supervisor when he gets home tonight. He names the person and the workplace and appears resolute. Which of the following is the physician's most appropriate action?
options: Maintain absolute confidentiality regardless of what the patient discloses
Take reasonable steps to warn or protect the identifiable victim while preserving as much confidentiality as possible
Report every such statement to the police without individualized assessment
Discharge him and document that confidentiality was maintained
items.explanation: When a patient presents a serious and imminent threat to an identifiable person, the duty to protect overrides confidentiality through warning the potential victim, notifying authorities, or other reasonable steps, while disclosing only the information necessary to prevent harm.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: An 82-year-old woman with advanced dementia and metastatic cancer is admitted with pneumonia and respiratory failure. She has a valid, signed living will stating that she does not want mechanical ventilation, and she has no available surrogate. Which of the following is most appropriate?
options: Honor the advance directive and provide comfort-focused care
Intubate because the directive might not apply to pneumonia
Wait for a court order before acting on the directive
Ask the bedside nurse to decide whether the directive applies
items.explanation: A valid advance directive expressing the patient's wishes about life-sustaining treatment should be followed when she lacks capacity, and a prior competent refusal is not overridden because the acute illness is potentially treatable. Clear applicable documents do not require court review or a nurse's judgment.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman seen on the first day of moderate low back pain without red flags asks for an MRI because she is worried something is seriously wrong. Examination shows intact strength, sensation, and reflexes. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
options: Reassure her, recommend time-limited symptomatic care, and explain why imaging is not indicated now
Order the MRI because her preference should determine testing
Refer immediately for neurosurgical consultation
Start opioid analgesia until the MRI can be completed
items.explanation: Imaging in the first weeks of uncomplicated low back pain does not improve outcomes and can lead to incidental findings and unnecessary invasive follow-up. Education, symptomatic care, and clear return precautions are appropriate, with imaging reserved for red flags or failure to improve.
items.reference: USMLE Step 3 Content Outline - Medical Ethics and Patient Safety
